source: Foster and Wilson (2006) Reverse replay of behavioural sequences in hippocampal place cells during the awake state
finding: Abstract confirms rats replay recent spatial experience in temporally reversed order right after the run, and the authors tie it to reinforcement-learning-style evaluation of sequences.
numbers: No spike counts, event counts, compression factors or rat numbers could be obtained.
quote: recent episodes of spatial experience are replayed in a temporally reversed order
limits: The Nature page is paywalled (preview and abstract only) and PubMed holds only the abstract. Gap 4 stays open for numbers. Do not cite any F&W 2006 figure from this file.
agent_relevance: Use only as a pointer to the backward-credit operator; numbers must come from a paper that quotes them.

source: Foster (2017) Replay Comes of Age (Annual Review of Neuroscience)
finding: Review of replay content, about 421 citations per OpenAlex. Full text was not reachable (the site returned an HTML wall); not read.
numbers: none captured
limits: Unread. Gap 4 for Foster 2017 stays open.
agent_relevance: None until read.

source: Olafsdottir, Carpenter, Barry (2017) Task demands predict a dynamic switch in the content of awake hippocampal replay (Neuron)
finding: Replay content depends on engagement. Just after arriving at, or just before leaving, a reward corner, replay favours the current direction and the nearby arms. During longer stops that bias vanishes. Task-focused events before a turn predict whether the turn is correct.
numbers: 8 rats, 6 m Z-track, 24 sessions, mean 22 laps. 1,415 engaged and 3,010 disengaged events. Engaged: 62.26% direction-congruent (p<0.0001), 80.70% local-arm (p<0.0001). Disengaged: 52.19% (p=0.39) and 71.42% (p=0.31). Engaged vs disengaged p<0.0001. Classifier on engaged events before turns: 60.3% accuracy (p=0.02 vs shuffle); disengaged 55.2% (p=0.09). Mean 8.88 wrong turns per session.
quote: hippocampal reactivations dynamically and abruptly switch between operational modes in response to task demands
limits: Prediction accuracy is modest (60.3%) and errors are few. Engagement and time since stopping are confounded with position. Deep entorhinal grid cells replay coherently with CA1 only in disengaged immobility.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence for gap 5: the same animal in the same task switches between a plan-like mode near action points and a consolidate-like mode in long idle periods. Suggests the agent should plan at decision points and consolidate during idle time, not use one mode.

source: Eldar, Lai, Dolan, Dayan (2020) The roles of online and offline replay in planning (eLife)
finding: Human MEG study. The more flexible a person's choices, the more they replayed trajectories during the task, and that replay was coupled with re-planning. The less flexible, the more they replayed previously preferred trajectories during rest. Online and offline replay support different strategies.
numbers: N=40 subjects. Post-outcome decodability higher in subjects with more on-task sequenceness (r=0.32, p=0.04, permutation). Coping with reward change vs position change partial rho=0.50, p=0.001. Flexibility vs reaction time of second moves r=-0.61, p<0.001. Map-sketch accuracy r=0.51, p<0.001.
quote: online and offline replay both participate in planning but support distinct decision strategies
limits: Human MEG sequenceness is indirect. Correlational across people. One task.
agent_relevance: Second line for gap 5: on-task replay goes with replanning and flexibility, off-task replay goes with rehearsing the already preferred path (habit-like). An idle-time pass that only re-reads preferred answers may entrench rather than improve.

source: Mattar and Daw (2018) Prioritized memory access explains planning and hippocampal replay (Nat Neurosci)
finding: Normative model: memories are replayed in order of Need times Gain (how soon a state will be visited, and how much better choices become). In a gridworld, prioritized replay learns faster than random-order Dyna replay and than no replay. Reverse replay arises where Gain is high (after a new reward), forward replay where Need is high (before departure).
numbers: Prioritized agent needs fewer steps per trial than random-replay Dyna and a model-free agent in the simulated mazes (no single headline figure captured from the text). Reproduces many place-cell replay findings qualitatively.
quote: ordered by utility: how much extra reward would be earned due to better choices
limits: Simulation only, small gridworlds, no LLM. Need and Gain require a model of the world and known values.
agent_relevance: Gives a rule for what the agent should revisit: states likely to be needed soon and where new information changes the best action. Test against random review (gap 7); this is gridworld support only.

source: Farooq and Dragoi (2019) Emergence of preconfigured and plastic time-compressed sequences in early postnatal development (Science)
finding: Naive rat pups show preplay-like trajectory sequences in sleep before first track experience from postnatal day 17-18 on, growing to extended trajectories by P19-20. Experience-dependent replay exceeds preplay only at P23-24.
numbers: Recording from the first day after eye opening. No trajectory sequences at P15-P16 (stationary location frames instead; about 16% of awake-rest frames). Replay larger than preplay at P23-P24 (P<0.009, t test). Within-day experience effect at P15-16: P=0.92 (n=3 and 4 animals). Location decoding error about 10% of track length at P15-16, about 5% at P23-24.
quote: preconfigured trajectory-like sequences from persistent, location-depicting ensembles during postnatal week 3
limits: Same lab as Dragoi and Tonegawa 2011 and 2013, so not an independent replication. Small animal numbers per age group. Shuffles and templates still decide what counts.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 partial: supports an innate scaffold of sequences that experience then selects from. The agent analogy is a prior template library plus selection, not generation from nothing.

source: Backbone spiking sequence as a basis for preplay, replay, and default states in human cortex (Nat Commun 2023)
finding: Human temporal-lobe single units show an average backbone spiking sequence identified during pre-task rest that stays stable across cognitive states, with rigid and flexible elements. Flexible elements promote memory specificity.
numbers: Numbers not extracted (abstract and introduction read only). Human single-unit recordings during an episodic memory task.
quote: pre-existing network dynamics serve as a scaffold for ongoing neural activity in the human cortex
limits: Cortical, not hippocampal place-cell preplay. Defines preplay as pre-task sequence stability, a looser notion than the Dragoi trajectory test. Patient population.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: extends the pre-existing-sequence idea to humans but is a weaker and different test. Do not count as a replication of Silva or Dragoi.

source: Carvalho, Hall-McMaster, Lee, Gershman (2025) Preemptive Solving of Future Problems: Multitask Preplay in Humans and Machines (arXiv 2507.05561)
finding: Algorithm that replays experience on one task as counterfactual simulation of other tasks that were reachable but not pursued. Predicts people's reuse of past paths and beats model-free, Dyna and goal-relabelling methods on generalisation in a grid world and in Craftax.
numbers: Human experiments N=100 each, preregistered. Exp 1 path reuse 62.39% (95% CI 53.99-69.53), p=0.0049 vs 50%. Exp 2 reuse 62.80%; Universal Value Functions 0% success, Universal Landmark SFs 7.65%, HER 5.56%, depth-first search path reuse 39.00%; Multitask Preplay 97.74% success, 99.50% reuse. Later experiment: Multitask Preplay 97.5% success, 99.3% reuse; HER 8.22%. Craftax: generalises to 10,000 new environments while Dyna and model-free methods plateau below that, at fixed 1M steps.
quote: counterfactual simulation of an accessible but unpursued task
limits: Grid-world and Craftax, not language tasks. The 'preplay' is a counterfactual-simulation algorithm named by analogy, not a hippocampal recording. The authors say goal relabelling gives no advantage in Craftax.
agent_relevance: Closest AI test of the preplay idea: use spare compute to pre-solve tasks you could have chosen. For the agent: after a problem, pre-solve nearby variants and cache the paths. Needs a language-task test at equal tokens.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time (arXiv 2504.13171), predictability section
finding: Gap 3 boundary check in full text. Sleep-time gain relies on shared structure between context and query. The authors state that where queries are hard to predict or unrelated to the context, sleep-time compute will be less effective and normal test-time scaling may be better.
numbers: Predictability measured as log-probability of the question given the context under Llama2-70B base; the accuracy gap between sleep-time and test-time compute widens in higher-predictability quantile bins (five bins) on Stateful GSM-Symbolic P1 and P2. No test on genuinely unpredictable reasoning queries.
quote: In settings where the queries are challenging to predict or unrelated to the context, sleep-time compute will be less effective.
limits: Predictability and difficulty are confounded in their own examples (predictable questions were simpler). Datasets are split math problems. No open-ended reasoning measured.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 stays half-closed: direction shown (gain grows with predictability) but no measured zero-gain point. Agent should gate idle precompute on a predictability estimate.

source: Song et al. (2026) Hippo: Training-Free Agent Self-Evolution via Hippocampal Replay (arXiv 2610.24453)
finding: Memory framework that compares several attempts at the same task, then merges and revises stored lessons with applicability conditions. Plain accumulation of lessons rises, then falls below the no-memory baseline. Ablations separate reflection, consolidation, cross-attempt comparison and update rule.
numbers: Base model GPT-5.6 Sol. WebArena 64.20 no memory to 72.90 Hippo; SWE-bench Verified 81.50 to 88.50. Without consolidated layer L2: 66.50 and 83.80. Without episodic reflection L1: 68.70 and 85.63. Separate summaries plus append-only 61.30; compare rollouts plus append-only 70.10; compare rollouts plus repeated rewrite 54.57; add-and-delete 72.90. Success/failure labels instead of surprise judge cost 1.8 to 8.5 points. Cost per task $1.93 to $2.17 (+12.4%); actor calls 69.27 to 74.75 (+7.9%). Eight rollouts per task; three benchmarks.
quote: accumulation baseline ... improves at first, then declines and eventually falls below the no-memory baseline
limits: Their own harness and judge. Compute is not matched to a retry arm: the paper reports no-memory at-least-once success of 73.6% over eight attempts on WebArena, close to Hippo's per-attempt 72.9%.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 and gap 1 partial: comparing attempts (a sleep-like consolidation) beats summarising single attempts by 8.8 points, and unrestricted rewriting hurts (54.57 vs 70.10 append-only). Consolidation needs rules, not free edits.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Contextual Experience Replay for Self-Improvement of Language Agents (ACL 2025)
finding: Training-free buffer of distilled environment dynamics and skills from past trajectories, retrieved in context. Improves the GPT-4o agent on WebArena by 51.0% relative.
numbers: WebArena success 24.3 (ReAct) to 33.4 offline, 33.2 online, 36.7 hybrid (relative +51.0%). Extra input tokens about 7.9K to 20.6K per task (Table 3). CER 31.4 vs CER using a ground-truth success filter 33.5 (Table 7). Forums split ablation: full 37.7, without skills 33.3, without dynamics 35.1. Needs goal-oriented trajectories; random exploration helps little.
limits: Not a replay ablation against fresh solving at equal tokens. Hybrid uses human-annotated trajectories. Failed trajectories mildly hurt.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: stored trajectory reuse gives a real gain but costs extra tokens and has two parts (dynamics, skills). Failed trajectories need filtering, which echoes reverse replay needing a reward signal.

source: Hajimiri et al. (2026) Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? (arXiv 2606.15017, EMNLP 2026)
finding: Under matched total tokens, a vanilla agent given extra steps matches or beats AWM, ASI and ReasoningBank in aggregate on WebArena across three models. Memory gains largely vanish against a budget-matched actor.
numbers: WebArena average success, Gemini 3 Flash: Vanilla-IB 44.78 (73.6K tokens), AWM 39.34 (99.3K), ASI 41.02 (107.3K), ReasoningBank 39.33 (82.6K). GPT-5.4-mini: 32.67 vs 27.02, 29.00, 24.58. Qwen 3.6-27B: 42.14 vs 38.01, 40.15, 37.00. WorkArena-L1 Qwen: Vanilla-IB 55.56, AWM 53.53, ASI 48.49, ReasoningBank 55.56. Three runs each. Reddit/Gemini: AWM ties Vanilla-IB at 15 steps.
limits: A later critical review (arXiv 2609.33153, seen only as a search snippet, not opened) says the vanilla control also got a longer step horizon and tree pruning, so extra steps are not fully isolated. Online setting couples results to task order.
agent_relevance: Strongest counter-evidence for gaps 7 and 8: memory and replay modules often lose to spending the same tokens on more acting. Any replay step in our agent must be tested against an equal-token retry arm.

source: Tan et al. (2026) Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents, HCAPO (arXiv 2603.08754)
finding: Uses the model itself as a post-hoc critic that sees the outcome and rescales step-level credit, a backward pass from outcome to earlier steps. It is a training-time RL method (changes weights), not a scaffold.
numbers: Qwen2.5-7B: ALFWorld success 77.6 (GRPO) to 91.4 (+13.8), 96.9 with temporal smoothing; GiGPO 90.8. WebShop success 66.1 to 73.8 (+7.7). 1.5B ALFWorld: 87.0 vs 72.8. Hindsight scoring is one forward pass over existing trajectories; the paper's latency breakdown gives it a small share (about 8.3% as read from the figure text). Averaged over 3 seeds.
limits: RL training, not an inference-time scaffold. No equal-token comparison against forward re-reading. The baseline GRPO has trajectory-level credit only.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 partial: backward credit assignment from the outcome helps when it changes learning, and is cheap to compute. No evidence yet for an inference-time version at equal tokens.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) AgenTracer: Who Is Inducing Failure in LLM Agentic Systems? (arXiv 2509.03312)
finding: Frontier LLMs are poor at locating the decisive wrong step in a failed multi-agent trajectory. Backward blame is hard, which limits any backward pass after a failed attempt.
numbers: Who&When handcraft subset, step-level accuracy with / without ground truth: Claude-Sonnet-4 20.68/20.68, Gemini-2.5-Pro 17.24/18.97, GPT-4.1 13.29/6.90, DeepSeek-R1 9.72/6.90. Automated subset step-level: Claude-Sonnet-4 42.86/37.30. Acting on flagged errors gave MetaGPT and MaAS gains of 4.8 to 14.2%.
limits: Multi-agent systems, not single-agent reasoning chains. The tracer is a trained 8B model. Step-level labels are few (Who&When 127 trajectories).
agent_relevance: Gap 1: a backward pass that has to name the culprit step will often name the wrong one. Cheap safeguard: require evidence for the blamed step and verify by replaying with that step changed.

source: Qian et al. (2026) Current Agents Fail to Leverage World Model as Tool for Foresight (arXiv 2601.03905, ACL 2026)
finding: When world-model simulation is available as a tool before acting, agents often do not use it, misuse the predicted rollouts, or get worse. The bottleneck is deciding when to simulate and how to use the result.
numbers: Some agents invoke simulation in fewer than 1% of cases; about 15% of predicted rollouts are misused; performance sometimes degrades by up to 5% when simulation is available or enforced. LLaMA variants are more willing than GPT and Qwen variants.
limits: Vision-language agents and learned world models, not text self-simulation. No equal-token comparison against act-then-revise.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: forward rollout is no free win. The agent needs a rule for when to roll out and a check on how the rollout result is used.

source: WebATLAS (2025) Memory-augmented web agent with look-ahead action simulation (arXiv 2510.22732)
finding: Training-free web agent with a cognitive map, high-level planner and look-ahead simulation of candidate actions before acting. Reaches 63.0 on WebArena-Lite with multi-site, above Plan-and-Act at 53.9.
numbers: AgentOccam base 47.9; Base+CM-Raw 44.8; Base+CM 57.4; Base+HL 50.9; full Base+CM+HL+LA 63.0 (67.1 without multi-site); WebPilot 35.3, AWM 33.0, WebRL 48.1 (without multi-site). The ablation table does not list Base+CM+HL without look-ahead, so look-ahead is not isolated.
limits: Workshop paper, no equal-token arm, small split, look-ahead not ablated alone despite the text claiming complementary components.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: rollout-before-acting appears in a winning system but is not isolated, and saturation was not measured. Treat as weak.

source: Momennejad et al. (2023) Evaluating Cognitive Maps and Planning in Large Language Models with CogEval (arXiv 2309.15129)
finding: Gap 9 closed with numbers. LLMs list graph edges well but fail at multi-step planning on community-structured graphs by hallucinating edges, taking longer paths and looping. BFS or DFS hints help only marginally.
numbers: Mean (SD) by condition, GPT-4: 1stepPath 0.99 (0.08), 2stepPath 0.82 (0.35), 3stepPath 0.55 (0.38), nstepPath 0.47 (0.38), policyReval 0.21 (0.18), rewardReval 0.67 (0.40), transReval 0.60 (0.42). GPT-3.5: 0.76, 0.73, 0.37, 0.31, 0.18, 0.57, 0.59. LLaMA-13B nstepPath 0.06; Bard 0.00. Shortest path to a state one cluster away: GPT-4 success 0 of 30 at temperature 0, at most 10% at other temperatures. Each condition run 30 times.
limits: 2023 models only. Newer reasoning models not tested. Scores are an Adjusted Rand Index style metric where 1.0 equals the Leiden algorithm. The paper calls the second number a standard error; treat as spread.
agent_relevance: Replay unrolls trajectories over a learned map. LLMs fail exactly at unrolling over a given map as it deepens. Supports giving the agent an explicit graph or notes to roll out over, and re-testing with current models.

source: Ma et al. (2026) Freshness-Aware Prioritized Experience Replay for LLM/VLM RL (arXiv 2604.16918)
finding: In RL post-training, plain prioritized replay degrades results because stored priorities go stale, but adding an age decay turns it into a gain over on-policy training.
numbers: FreshPER vs on-policy: +46% NQ Search, +367% Sokoban, +133% VLM FrozenLake; standard PER without decay consistently degrades. Eight tasks; 0.5B, 3B and 7B models.
limits: Weight-update RL, not an inference-time memory-review loop. The baseline is on-policy, not random replay of the same buffer.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 partial: priority needs a freshness term. By analogy, an idle-time review queue ordered by old scores will go stale unless age-discounted.

source: Arnal et al. (2026) Efficient RL Training for LLMs with Experience Replay (arXiv 2604.08706)
finding: A tuned replay buffer cuts LLM RL generation compute by up to about 40% with accuracy kept, and sometimes higher. Strict on-policy sampling is suboptimal when generation is costly.
numbers: Up to 40% compute saving at maintained accuracy. Theory trades staleness-induced variance, diversity and generation cost. Inference can exceed 80% of post-training GPU hours.
limits: Training-time. Which trajectories to replay (priority) is not the focus. Not an inference-time agent.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 and 8 context: reusing stored rollouts pays when generating them is expensive. The same logic suggests caching solved sub-problems at inference time.

source: Kim and Choi (2026) Hippocampal consolidation without replay in fully fine-tuned networks (arXiv 2611.01952)
finding: Hippocampus-inspired index of past input geometry limits weight movement and lets a network keep learning without cross-task replay, a teacher or inference-time memory. Argues replay is not the only route to consolidation.
numbers: Abstract level only read: claims gains over replay baselines DER++ and CLS-ER on continual-learning benchmarks; no figures captured.
limits: Continual learning of weights, not agent reasoning. Only abstract and first page read.
agent_relevance: Weak link. Shows replay can be substituted by a stored index, so replay's benefit in LLM agents should be isolated, not assumed.
